finding: §2.6's load-bearing safety claim — "The open findings remain in recorded state and still count against convergence" — is false for the review phase under tp's own convergence predicate, which §2.6 never says it changes. Review convergence is ReviewConsecutiveClean: it walks rounds from the newest backwards and stops at the first unclean round, so only TRAILING rounds decide convergence. §2.6 defines open for review as a surviving finding in ANY recorded round. A finding stranded in round 4 therefore has no effect on whether rounds 5 and 6 are clean. It is precisely the deactivation that strands it: an active role would re-report the defect each round and keep the round unclean, and a deactivated role emits nothing, so the spec converges with the open finding still sitting in an earlier round file. The sentence is what makes 'report, not refuse' safe, and it is not true.
